hero.subtitle: When a death in St. Helena was caused by someone else's carelessness, your family has the right to answers and to a civil claim under California law. LawProactive connects you, at no cost, with an independent wrongful death attorney who serves Napa County.

about.title: St. Helena Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: St. Helena is a small town of about 5,469 people, and when someone here dies because of another's carelessness, the loss ripples through the whole community. Public collision records for 2016, the most recent final year, list 24 injury crashes and 31 people hurt along Main Street, Route 29, Oak Avenue and the Silverado Trail. Wrongful death claims in Napa County don't come only from the road, though. A fall on a poorly kept property, a medical error, a defective product, or a workplace incident can leave a family facing questions no one wants to ask. California law lets certain survivors — a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then dependent heirs — bring a civil claim for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. That claim runs separately from any criminal case. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm; we connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why St. Helena Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a government entity is involved. Reaching out sooner keeps every option open.

items.title: Full picture of recoverable losses
items.desc: A claim can cover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Attorneys in our network take these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My loved one died in a crash on Route 29 near St. Helena. Does it matter that it's a state highway?
items.answer: It can. Route 29 is a public highway, and if your family believes a road design or maintenance issue played a role, any claim against a government entity carries a much shorter filing window than the standard two years. An independent attorney can review the police report and collision records quickly to determine whether that shorter deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, separate from any prosecution in Napa County. A criminal conviction is not required to bring a civil claim, and a criminal acquittal does not automatically end one. Your attorney can explain how the two proceedings may affect each other.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm, and what does it cost to get connected?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects St. Helena families with an independent personal injury attorney who handles wrongful death cases. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and there is never a charge for the connection itself.
